notes.title: Playtest build April 2025 now live!
notes.content:
Hello captains! We have a new playtest build with some big updates on the hook for ya.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44951977/a8963fd9799d6af845404299460a6767eb5c2381.png[/img]

[h1]New features[/h1]
[list]
[*] Save games! Not the most exciting feature but something that has taken a lot of effort to get in. You can now open the pause menu when not in the tutorial or combat to save the game. The game is also saved when entering and leaving a harbour.
[*] A new Rift has been spotted out at sea! This one is still in development but we would like your feedback on what we have made so far. We are quite excited to hear what you think.
[*] New starting ship: The glass cannon Tarpon
[*] Rumours now have their own page in the journal
[*] Streamlined creating your captain
[*] More things to take with you in the life boat when starting a new run
[*] You can now name your ship when starting a new run
[*] More narrative content
[*] More sound effects
[*] More crew traits
[*] More Auxiliary Equipment with a wider range of effects
[*] Traits and Auxiliary Equipment now impact challenge difficulty
[*] Crew responding to one of their crew mates dying or being marooned
[/list]

[h1]Bug fixes[/h1]
[list]
[*] Captain no longer leaves because of low mood. Thanks for reporting it @Rasmus and @copakindred!
[/list]

[h1]Known issues[/h1]
[list]
[*] Crew for hire gets shuffled if exiting the Inn, even though you have bought them drinks
[*] Occasionally monsters fly in the tutorial
[*] Log entries do not not get saved
[/list]

[h1]Unknown issues?[/h1]
[list]
[*] Probably a lot of fun bugs with save games we haven’t found yet. Do jump on our Discord and tell us if you find any :D 
[/list]

Looking forward to hear what you think!

- Skipper Alex

notes.title: Playtest build February 2025 now live!
notes.content:
Ahoy freebooters we are back with another playtest. Here's the new stuff:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44778071/d4b80d2ba3620606692b5504cb881a8eda9c7eb0.gif[/img]
[h2]New features[/h2]
- Different starting ships. When starting a game you now get to pick which type of ship you want to play as
- New starting ship the Beluga: A heavy freighter bristling with turrets
- New main quest that points the player towards the Great Rift
- More content for Red Tides
- More variety to challenges
- Changed controller input scheme so you now fire guns with the right trigger. Sails are deployed/hoisted with DPad Up/Down
- Separate reload sounds for each weapon type
- Increased the amount of available crew in harbours by 2
- Rebalanced character traits
- Character traits can now affect difficulties of tasks in a challenge
- Hover explainer in challenge to show how the chance a crewmember adds to a task is calculated
- Particle effects have gotten an overhaul
- Towns now also have weapon shops
- Improvements to the tutorial
- Improvements to the UI
- More types of news articles can be found in the newspaper
- More iteration on new ship physics
- Warning message when running out of ammunition thanks for the suggestion @CthulhuFhtaghn!

[h2]Bug fixes[/h2]
- Exposure quest has been fixed. Thanks to @cornsalsa for reporting it!
- You the captain will no longer leave due to low mood. Thanks to @rasmus and @copakindred for reporting it!
- Skill Point Assignment Bug. Thanks to @Why No Rhinos for reporting it!
- Quest Text Overlap bug. Thanks to @Why No Rhinos for reporting it!
- Was hard to get mouse hover on the crewmember portrait in the duties journal page. Thanks to @CthulhuFhtaghn for reporting it!
- Various fixes to make hitting enemies easier

[h2]Known issues[/h2]
- Ships physics are still sometimes a bit wonky 

It's always rewarding to write the changelist and see all the stuff we managed to get done in the past month. I hope you will like the improvements and looking forward to hear what you think!

Safe winds
- Captain Alex

notes.title: Playtest build January 2025
notes.content:
Ahoy freebooters
We are live with a new build! There's been a big overhaul to combat and challenges.

[h3]New features[/h3]
- Big graphical overhaul to the UI
- Ships use a better physics model so they ride waves better
- New aiming method where you can always fire cannons and adjust level of auto aim in the options menu
- New weapon: The fast motor cannon
- New weapon: The experimental convolution cannon that pushes enemies
- New weapon: The full pounder, a giant iron fist ram that lets you suckerpunch other ships!
- Challenges have been improved with new mechanics
- Do heists for the Shaped Folk
- Reworked how enemies spawn so it scales better with the intended difficulty
- A big chunk of vibes related to crew relations has been added
- Vibes now show portraits of involved crew
- Streamlined tutorial level layout to make it faster to complete
- Monsters have been moved over to new AI system
- And an ingame changelog if you fancy reading all of this twice

[h3]Bug fixes[/h3]
- Fixed quest targets could spawn inside floating settlements

[h3]Known issues[/h3]
- We have not set dressed the new tutorial level layout yet so that’s why it’s quite barren.
- The game now features "airships" and dancing patrol ships due to the new ship physics

Have fun and do let us know of any bugs on our Discord page or the forums.

Safe winds
Captain Alex

notes.title: Playtest Patch #5
notes.content:
Ahoy captains I just wanted to let you know I pushed a new update to the playtest build yesterday. Running a playtest on Steam is a bit quirky so the playtest has it's own news feed so here's a copy of the new stuff listed over there:
[h3]Changes[/h3]
[list]
[*] By popular demand you can now fire a single cannon by doing a short press of the fire button. Holding it down fires a full volley
[*] Controller: Took out the option to open/close the journal with the X button. This frees the button to do other input like assigning equipment and will also allow us to use it for more interesting combat
[*] Mouse input: Zooming has been inverted so scrolling towards you zooms out
[*] Option to invert zoom
[*] Better feedback when a rumour has been completed
[*] In the map the name of the active quest is shown underneath the marker to make it easier to figure out what quest it is for
[*] When entering port there's now a message telling you how many wages you have to pay before you can leave the port
[*] Tutorial now teaches zooming and sail turning better
[*] Easier to understand how to assign equipment
[*] Game economy has been rebalanced to be harder
[*] Tweaked turning so it's more snappy especially for keyboard
[/list]
[h3]Fixes[/h3]
[list]
[*] Inverted default direction for zooming when using mouse and keyboard
[*] Can use right mouse button to unassign stamina for Duties
[*] Ship points towards sea when starting a new game
[*] Needler projectiles doesn't collide with wind zones any more
[*] Exposure swirls doesn't collide with wind zones any more
[*] Fixed issue where a bunch of rumours would not be available
[/list]

As always we want to hear what you think of the game so hit us up here in the Steam forum or on our Discord, it works better than trying to send us a letter in a bottle ;)

Safe winds and happy holidays
- Captain Alex

notes.title: Thanks for your feedback! Here's what's next
notes.content:
Ahoy captains it's been great seeing you enjoying the latest playtest and come with suggestions for what can be improved. I've looked over all the feedback including the Let's Play videos (damn we suddendly got some traction!) and have come up with this list which is what we will focus on in the next month or so:

[h3]Tutorial & gameplay verbs not taught well[/h3]
[list]
[*] Zooming. Fix: Show hint in tutorial, rightside permanent hint, start camera a bit zoomed out
[*] Turning sails. Fix: Move that part of the tutorial to be after lode anchor when sailing to port, rightside permanent hint
[*] Difficult to understand sails are not fully deployed. Fix: Make the input a bit snappier, tutoriali\e it better
[*] Bits of the journal can be accessed too soon. Fix: Disable them until reaching the first port
[*] Difficult to understand how to install equipment. Fix: Hint directly in the hover text
[/list]
[h3]Keyboard+mouse input wonky[/h3]
[list]
[*] Cannot use ESC as back action Fix: have it work as back button until the only logical step is to open the Pause menu
[*] One player would like to invert zoom when scrolling
[*] Be able to right click to unassign stamina points
[/list]
[h3]Quests & Map[/h3]
[list]
[*] If marker is outside edge of map difficult to know where to go. Fix: Dotted line to marker
[*] If having multiple quests it is not obvious what quest is active. Fix: Have quest headline underneath map marker
[/list]
[h3]Ease of use[/h3]
[list]
[*] Using the back action as a third UI option to for example install equipment is not intuitive. Fix: Assign new keybindings to it for controller and keyboard
[*] Be able to invert zoom input in Options
[*] Need better feedback crew has to get paid. Fix: Add a hint label to the harbour overview UI that the player needs to pay the crew before they can leave.
[*] No feedback when a rumour has been followed up on: Fix: Small XP reward when chasing up rumour and list it in the captain's log
[*] Crew member status widgets does not highlight text
[*] Morning duties assignment gets tedious to do again and again. Fix: Make animation faster, select the lock in button to start with
[/list]
[h3]Balancing[/h3]
[list]
[*] Economy is a too generous. Fix: Make quests pay less
[/list]
[h3]Combat[/h3]
[list]
[*] Need to make combat more varied. Fix: I got a bunch of ideas how to fix this that all tie into each other so will share more at a later point
[/list]
[h3]Not being able to tilt camera up above horizon line[/h3]
[list]
[*] Will be time consuming to solve in terms of technical issues with draw distance and rendering the horizon but worth testing out how it would make the game feel if the camera was more free and then decide if we want to make the change
[/list]
We are planning on releasing another build this week with some of these fixes in and enable access to the playtest again. 

Safe winds
- Captain Alex

notes.title: New playtest: Visit the Shaped Folk
notes.content:
Ahoy freebooters! We are back with another playtest! Lots of new stuff and improvements have been made and we would love to get your feedback on them.

notes.title: June's playtest sails into view
notes.content:
Ahoy captains! We are back with a new playtest build full of additions and fixes to the game. These are:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44778071/d862e80c4e4aeec030f79955585518ca549365e7.png[/img]
New stuff:
[list]
[*] Reactive vibes! The text describing what happens aboard the ship are now much more tailored to the crew and can also affect the game. This makes the crew come much more alive.
[*] New shop UI that makes it easy to buy more more than one item at a time and just looks a lot better
[*] Updated main menu UI
[*] When visiting a port you can now decide if it should be the return target for the Lode Anchor
[*] Tutorial has been streamlined so you first learn about assigning duties after reaching the first harbour
[*] Renderscale setting in options menu to help with performance on lower end graphics cards and at high resolutions. Could be beneficial for playing on a Steamdeck as well to help out with battery life
[*] The traits you create your captain with has been rewritten to fit better with the world building
[*] Ambition trait. When creating your captain you also have to decide why they are seeking The Great Rift
[*] Various visual improvements
[*] You now start with fever provisions
[*] More balancing
[*] Better way of selecting resolutions in options menu (thanks for reporting it @LuxiePotato)
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44778071/67dae64de17876fa6efc05a16d46680207575ec0.png[/img]
Fixes
[list]
[*] Equipment can now be sold in shops
[*] Intro text fades in better (thanks for reporting it @LuxiePotato)
[*] UI fixes related to shop UI and the event UI
[*] Notifications show when journal is open even in harbour
[*] Taking the same quest type like finding a missing ship from the same harbour now gives you a new location to get to
[*] Various smaller bug fixes
[/list]

Looking forward to hear what you think!

Captain Alex

notes.title: Dev Log 5 - Preparing for our first showcase
notes.content:
Hello, we are back with another dev log. This time, with an update on what we have been up to over the last couple of weeks and some news about our first public showcase!

[h1]Ship and monster models 2.0[/h1]
Sofie, our artist, has been busy getting updated models for ships and monsters into the game, as we are aiming for a more gritty visual tone than what we initially had. The pirate faction in the game is also using captured ships from other factions, so we have been working on how to portray that. Yes, this is an Imperial ship but it is being crewed by seagoing scoundrels, so we show this by painting them in more rusty and grimy colors.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44778071/c11054968582fa3ef6153c4abbd3de952dd482ad.png[/img]

The ship hulls have also been updated to have more pronounced silhouettes to make them look less cute at a distance.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44778071/a756f59837040553a71300ebae0f362d10e38f23.png[/img]

The Needler enemy also got a redesign to look more fierce and hostile. Sofie has drawn inspiration from deep-sea anglerfish in her redesign. It’s quite scary-looking, if I should say so myself!

[h1]Preparing for our first showcase[/h1]
We have been selected to showcase Sea Of Rifts at Copenhagen Gaming Week in the upcoming weekend, which is quite exciting since it’s the first time we will show the game to the public. Some work has gone into polishing the game, with our writer Fergus getting familiar with the in-house tools Alex has created to make narrative content for the game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44778071/a0b0523b14156e94907dc505192a92ec8a274a23.png[/img]
[i]A writer stoically facing his worst fear, the empty page[/i]

On top of that, we also wanted to have something that would draw people into our booth and therefore decided to make a custom rudder controller for the game! The next blog post will be about how it was showcasing the game and will go into more detail on how we built the controller and got it connected to the game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44778071/de5717789c5971a15a087769ccb94462beba4e76.png[/img]

That’s all for this time. Please give us a wishlist if you haven’t already :)

notes.title: Dev Log 3 - NPC ships, ahoy!
notes.content:
Hello, landlubbers! It’s Alex back with another dev update. This time, it’s about our newest gameplay feature: NPC ships!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44778071/dc10b2c9bd3087300ff981021da26ea0895606be.gif[/img]
[h1]What zombies and sea monsters have in common[/h1]
Have you ever thought about why zombies are so popular in video games? I think one reason is that they are easy to code. If you see a zombie do something that puts them in danger, it doesn’t go against the way we imagine a zombie to behave, since they are primarily driven by their lust for tasty brains. For the same reason, when I was prototyping Sea Of Rifts, I also started out with making monsters chase the player instead of other ships. It was simply easier and quicker to make than ships, since we expect a vessel crewed by other humans to behave more intelligently than a monster just following instinct.

This meant the combat could be prototyped quicker, but I also found out that they don’t make for interesting antagonists in the more narrative sense, since they can’t have as much character as other ships. With other ships, the player can build a relationship with the other captain and to the factions that they belong to. Since we are working towards having the game generate deeper stories, we therefore needed NPC ships.

I started out with defining the requirements for the system to drive the behavior of the ships:

- Use a common data structure so both the player and NPCs use the same data for their ships and weapons.
- Not too complicated to write.
- Something that can be extended with more behaviors as need be.
- Ships from different factions can interact with each other without involvement from the player.
- Didn’t need to be super performant since I don’t think we will have a lot of ships on screen at the same time

Therefore I split the system up into three groups: decision making, locomotion, and combat:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44778071/9ae9ceb77643e7f0e204e93f1576f1c0d79c9b52.png[/img]
For the decision making, I ended up with a mixture of boid steering used for simulating flocking behaviors and utility AI. If you are interested, AI In Games has a [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=p3Jbp2cZg3Q]great video[/url] on utility AI by the way. It also took some refactoring of the existing code used to steer the player ship to make it modular and plug into the steering code. The end system consists of a ship controller component that finds the behavior that has the highest utility and then uses the movement components to apply that movement.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44778071/2a8b1e77b56d4133c7dcd14041bc7e1513e79273.png[/img]
As you can see at the start of this post, it has worked out quite well! It’s going to be fun when we have more ships and factions in the game to tune the behavior so each ship gets to have more personality.

That’s it for this time! Please give us a wishlist if you haven’t already :)

notes.title: Dev Log 2 - No More Cute Boats!
notes.content:
Hello hello mateys! It is Alex again this time with a little update on what we have been busy with the last couple of weeks.

[h1]SHIP SILHOUETTE DESIGN [/h1]
 [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44778071/84c011edbe19548e5fab867dd3b714831fa24066.png[/img] 
We are currently working on adding NPC ships into the game. Our artist Sofie is therefore busy with working on the silhouettes for them. One tricky thing is we don’t want the ships to look cute- which is proving to be a challenge! With the top down perspective things are quite small on the screen and small things automatically look cute. Think for example chibi figures from manga and anime. Sofie has therefore tried designing some new silhouettes, that are a bit more twisted and aggressive to get away from that. As she wrote on our team slack:

 [center]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44778071/a9160b44c9c0e16fbd65127e922c240d5ef24223.png[/img]
 [/center]

[h1]MAP UPDATES[/h1]
A new feature that was also added recently is the map is now slowly revealed. A fog of discoverability if you will to half borrow a term from strategy games.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44778071/1d1eec552a668a1b95240542e6b449b244d41a31.png[/img]

This makes exploration a lot more interesting, since the player gets the satisfaction of revealing where they have been on the map. It's also a great way to show the player where they haven't been yet. Still needs some iteration to look prettier but I’m going to focus on adding NPC ships next so Sofie has something to test her new ship art with.

[h1]BUG FIXING, PLAYTESTING AND ITERATING ON THE TUTORIAL[/h1]
This week I also did a playtest. It's been about a month since the last time we tested so it was about time to get feedback on the game again. The tester is a fellow game designer, so there were a lot of good ideas on how to make the tutorial better, and improve the readability of the game.
[center]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44778071/4fc8708f7b3a3051c3d295a8dc41a5104c476f9b.gif[/img]
[/center]
That's it for this time. Merry Christmas from me and the rest of the team! If you want to give us a gift then consider wishlisting the game :)
